title: UK ETS aviation record-retention and audit QA controls

sources.title: UK Emissions Trading Scheme for aviation: how to comply

sources.publisher: Department for Energy Security and Net Zero
sources.title: Participating in the UK ETS

facts.source_fact: Regulators can carry out periodic audits of annual aviation emissions reports.
Relevant data and information must be retained for at least 10 years.
In practice the 10-year retention period runs from the report submission date.
The retention requirement includes data used to prepare the report even when that data becomes older than 10 years.
Operators are advised to prepare for annual reporting during the final quarter of the scheme year.
The annual emissions-report task appears in the METS work queue on 1 January of the following year.
Annual report data should be rounded in accordance with the Monitoring and Reporting Regulation.
facts.expected_handling: Apply the specified rounding rule, not ad hoc rounding.

facts.source_fact: The completed verified annual emissions report must be submitted by 31 March.
facts.expected_handling: Keep audit records tied to the submitted version.

facts.source_fact: A report is not formally submitted until the final METS submission step is completed.
facts.expected_handling: Do not treat draft or verifier-returned status as formal submission.

facts.source_fact: Audit and record-retention obligations concern operator reporting evidence, not parcel-level measurement.
facts.expected_handling: Do not infer parcel values from audit status.

guard_patterns.handling: Tie records to submitted report version.
Distinguish draft, verified and formally submitted states.

generation_rule: CARTESIAN_PRODUCT facts x guard_patterns; 10 x 10 = 100 controls
